title: Hygiene and grooming
audience: Trainee or new worker on the window cleaning (all heights) track, working under supervision.
learningOutcomes: Perform hand hygiene at task transitions, after glove removal, after handling waste and before touching clean supplies.
Start work with clean clothing, hands and hair, and cover minor cuts according to site policy.
Report illness, symptoms or exposure through workplace procedures rather than self-diagnosing.

instruction.heading: Exterior, height and access context
instruction.body: This lesson is part of the window cleaning (all heights) track. The track covers ground-level, water-fed pole and elevated access work on glazing and frames. Any work above ground level, or from a ladder, scaffold or elevating work platform, is restricted: it needs employer authorisation under a site-specific risk assessment, and the worker must hold any licence the relevant state or territory requires for the equipment used. This lesson does not grant the right to work at height or on solar systems.

instruction.heading: Overview
instruction.body: This lesson develops practical competence in hygiene and grooming for routine professional cleaning work. Apply the employer’s site procedures and stop if a task falls outside your training or authority.

instruction.heading: Instruction
instruction.body: Keep hands, nails, hair and clothing hygienic; follow infection-control and food-site rules without imposing unnecessary appearance requirements.

instruction.heading: Prepare and verify
instruction.body: Begin work with clean clothing and hands; keep nails and hair suitable for hygienic tasks and equipment safety. Cover minor cuts according to site policy and avoid working with exposed wounds.

instruction.heading: Perform the work safely and professionally
instruction.body: Perform hand hygiene at task transitions, after glove removal, after handling waste and before touching clean supplies. Keep eating, drinking and personal belongings away from cleaning chemicals and contaminated areas.

instruction.heading: Check, record and escalate
instruction.body: Change contaminated clothing safely and avoid carrying soil between sites. Follow workplace instructions for illness, symptoms or exposure reporting rather than attempting to diagnose yourself.

instruction.heading: Stop-work rule
instruction.body: Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

procedure: Start work with clean clothing, clean hands, and hair and nails suitable for hygienic tasks.
Cover minor cuts according to site policy, and avoid working with exposed wounds.
Perform hand hygiene at task transitions, after removing gloves, after handling waste and before touching clean supplies.
Keep eating, drinking and personal belongings away from cleaning chemicals and contaminated areas.
Change contaminated clothing safely, and avoid carrying soil between sites.
Follow the infection-control and food-site rules at the site.
Report illness, symptoms or exposure through workplace procedures rather than diagnosing yourself.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Licence and height notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work at height, on roofs, from elevated work platforms, or on solar systems. Completing it is not a licence, certificate or authority for regulated work. Boom-type elevating work platforms need a high risk work licence in Victoria at any boom length, and in New South Wales, Queensland, Tasmania, the Northern Territory and Western Australia where the boom is 11 metres or more. The WorkSafe WA page (last updated 13 August 2026) and the NT WorkSafe bulletin (no date shown) both state the 11-metre threshold. Check whether this work needs a high-risk work licence with the state regulator before you start. Queensland's definition does not cover platforms under 11 metres (WorkSafe Queensland page, no date shown). Tasmania's WP licence applies where the boom length is 11 metres or more, and no licence is needed for a boom under 11 metres (WorkSafe Tasmania page, last updated 1 December 2023). In New South Wales and Queensland the boom length is 11 metres: a boom-type platform of 11 metres or more needs the licence, and a shorter boom may not need it in those states. Victoria's WP class has no boom-length threshold, so the licence is not limited by length there. This lesson does not grant a licence. Scissor lifts need no high risk work licence in Victoria or the Northern Territory. Check the licence rules for your state or territory and obtain your employer's written authorisation before any work above ground level.

Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

qualityStandard: Hands are washed at each mandatory stage, such as before handling clean stock.
Work starts with clean clothing, hands and hair, and minor cuts are covered under site policy.
Eating, drinking and personal belongings are kept away from chemicals and contaminated areas.
Illness, symptoms or exposure are reported through workplace procedures.
summary: Hand hygiene is performed at task transitions, after glove removal, after handling waste and before touching clean supplies.
Work starts with clean clothing and hands, and hair and nails are kept suitable for hygienic tasks and equipment safety.
Illness, symptoms or exposure are reported through workplace procedures rather than self-diagnosed.

knowledgeChecks.question: What should you do if a hygiene risk is beyond your training?
options: Use a stronger product to clear it
Stop, and escalate to the supervisor
Keep working and judge the risk yourself
Ask a colleague if you should go on

knowledgeChecks.question: How should soiled clothing be handled before you travel to the next site?
options: Carry the contaminated clothing home to wash it in the car on the way home
Change and bag contaminated clothing safely, and avoid carrying soil to the next site
Wear it to the next site and leave it on in the van and wear it all day there
Leave it in the clean-storage cupboard beside the clean clothes for the team

knowledgeChecks.question: When must hand hygiene be performed during a cleaning task?
options: Only at the end of the shift and again before the first job of the next day
Only when hands look visibly dirty and not after gloves are removed
After removing gloves, after handling waste, and before touching clean supplies
Only when the client asks and not during the task itself or after waste handling

knowledgeChecks.question: Which habit is unsafe near the chemical store?
options: Eating a snack near the chemical store and contaminated area
Changing contaminated clothing before leaving the site
Keeping personal belongings away from chemicals
Covering a minor cut according to site policy

knowledgeChecks.question: How should an exposure or symptom be reported on site?
options: Report the exposure or symptoms through the workplace channel, as its instructions require
No record is needed for minor symptoms and the worker can handle it privately
Tell nobody, so the rota is not changed and carry on with the shift as normal
A note to yourself on your phone and a copy sent to a friend at work each day
